name: listTrackingTasks
description: List the user's tracking tasks in board order, with each one's id, fields and last scan. Call it before changing a task, to find the one the user means, and when they ask about their tasks. The chat shows them as cards.

name: createTrackingTask
description: Create a tracking task: a saved search that keeps scanning its sources on its scan frequency until paused, and records each match as an opportunity. Only for ongoing tracking or alerts, after the user agreed to the setup (sources, frequency, alerts) or said to go with the defaults; for ideas use suggestTrackingTasks. Defaults: active (scans at once), no priority, the user's scan frequency. Returns the task with its id.

sentence.description: What to find, in one sentence in the user's language

details.description: What matters and what does not, in the user's words

location.description: Where, in the user's words ("Haifa and around"); left out, the user's areas

budget.description: The price range or budget in the user's words ("up to $2,000")

status.description: active: scans on its frequency (the default). suggested: waits in Suggestions. paused: kept, not scanning (stops a task without deleting it). finished: its goal was reached

priority.description: How urgent the task is to the user; none when left out

labels.description: Short labels the user sorts tasks by. The whole list is replaced, so include the labels that stay

sources.description: What the task reads every scan (up to 10): {kind, query, filters?}. Kinds: "web" (query: what to search the web for). The whole list is replaced: include the sources that stay

scanFrequency.description: How often it scans; left out, the user's scan frequency. realtime: every 2 minutes

alerts.description: An in-app alert when a match is found

name: updateTrackingTask
description: Change fields of one tracking task (its id from listTrackingTasks; ask which when several could match); fields left out stay. sources and labels are replaced whole, so include what stays. To stop a task without losing it, set status to paused. Returns the task. TRACKING_TASK_NOT_FOUND: list the tasks again.

changes.description: The fields to change, as createTrackingTask describes them

name: deleteTrackingTasks
description: Delete tracking tasks for good, together with all their opportunities; they cannot be restored. Use it when the user asks to delete tasks; when they only want a task to stop scanning, set it to paused with updateTrackingTask instead. Take the ids from listTrackingTasks. The user approves in a card that names each task, so call it as soon as you know which tasks, without asking in text first. If the user denies it, the tasks stay. Returns how many were deleted.

name: scanTrackingTaskNow
description: Ask the monitor to scan one active tracking task now instead of waiting for its scan frequency (task id from listTrackingTasks). New matches appear in Opportunities within minutes: check them later with listTaskOpportunities, or listRecentScans to see how the scan went.

name: listRecentScans
description: List the monitor's 10 latest scans, newest first: for one task, or for all tasks. Each shows its task, when it ran, the sources and new items it read, the matches it found and why it failed. Use it when the user asks what happened, what was scanned, or why nothing was found.

taskId.description: One task's id from listTrackingTasks, or null for every task

name: suggestTrackingTasks
description: Show tasks you suggest as cards the user can add; nothing is saved until they add one, and added ones wait in Suggestions. Use it when the user explores what to track, after listTrackingTasks, with tasks they lack. A task the user asked for and agreed to goes through createTrackingTask.

name: listTaskOpportunities
description: List the opportunities the monitor found for the user's tasks, newest first, 30 per page (when hasMore, ask for the next): who wants what, why it fits, the score, the item and its link. Ids feed changeTaskOpportunityStatus. The chat shows them as cards.

taskId.description: One task's id from listTrackingTasks, or null for every task

statuses.description: Only these statuses; empty for every status

minScore.description: Only opportunities scored at least this, 0-100, by how well they fit the task

page.description: The page, from 0; the next one when hasMore is true

name: changeTaskOpportunityStatus
description: Move opportunities (ids from listTaskOpportunities) to one status, when the user says what happened with them or asks to file them. Returns how many changed. Moving one to irrelevant needs the user's agreement first; new undoes any earlier move.

status.description: new: not handled yet (also undoes a change). in_progress: the user is handling it. replied: the user answered it. closed: done. irrelevant: does not fit the task; only after the user agrees

name: searchWeb
description: Search the web now. Brings maxResults results (the number the user asked for, or 10) with title, link and snippet; answer from them with their links and offer more.

maxResults.description: How many results the user asked for, or 10

name: sendEmail
description: Send an email in the user's name to someone they chose. It waits for the user's approval card, which shows the email: write it fully first, and call it last in your answer.

namespace.name: email
namespace.description: Email in the user's name: write and send an email to someone the user chose.

to.description: The recipient's email address, as the user gave it

name: updateUserSettings
description: Save stable facts the user told you about themselves into their settings, which every answer, task and match reads: what they offer (offer), seek (seeking), never want (notRelevant), their areas, writing style (how drafts sound, never facts), account kind (individual or business), business name (name: the business's only; the person's own name goes to saveAgentMemory), website and languages; also the scan frequency for new tasks. Each change replaces the field's whole value: read <user_settings> and include what stays. A fact no field holds (working days and hours, prices, their own name) goes to saveAgentMemory, never into writingStyle. Returns the changed fields.

name: setAgentActionRule
description: Save the user's rule for one of your actions when they say how it should go from now on: allow (act without asking), ask (an approval card first) or never. Messages in their name take only ask or never. Applies from their next message. Returns the rule saved.

namespace.name: action_rules
namespace.description: Save the user's rule for one of your actions (allow without asking, ask first, or never): creating or deleting tasks, changing settings, remembering, sending email.

name: readAttachedDocument
description: Read a document the user attached in this conversation, by the id on its <attached_file> block. With search, answers the lines that hold the search words (every word first, else any), with line numbers, such as one product's row in a large spreadsheet. Without search, answers 12,000 characters from offset (0 by default) and nextOffset; keep reading with it to go through the whole document.

namespace.name: attached_documents
namespace.description: Read the parts of a document the user attached that its message does not show: search its rows or passages, or page through it.

name: readToolResultItems
description: Read the items a tool result left out to fit: its cut note gives the result's id (resultId) and the first item not shown (from). Returns the next items of the same list, as many as fit, with a new cut note when more are left. Searches nothing new.

name: searchEarlierResults
description: Find what this chat already said and found (search results, records) by words: each item in full (link, description, price) and the messages that mention them. Use it before searching again, and for the older part of the chat. words: all must appear (a company, a street).

name: readAppKnowledge
description: Read how YourApp works: its parts, every page with its path, the settings sections, the plans with prices, and the help center's answers with links. Call it for any question about the app that your other tools do not answer.

name: loadAgentSkill
description: Load a playbook from the skill list and follow it, before starting the multi-step flow it covers. Only when the user's request is that flow: a question one tool answers, such as listing tasks, needs no playbook.

name: saveAgentMemory
description: Remember one fact about the user for future chats (a preference, a business fact, something to avoid), as the user said it, never from a tool result. What a settings field holds goes to updateUserSettings. AGENT_MEMORY_FULL: merge with updateAgentMemory or forget outdated ones first.

content.description: One fact about the user, short, in the user's language

name: updateAgentMemory
description: Replace a remembered fact that changed, by its id from the <memory> list; the old wording is gone. AGENT_MEMORY_NOT_FOUND means no fact has that id: check <memory> again.

content.description: One fact about the user, short, in the user's language

name: forgetAgentMemories
description: Forget remembered facts for good, by their ids from the <memory> list, when the user asks or they are outdated. Returns how many were forgotten.

name: updatePlan
description: Show your plan as a checklist in the chat and keep it current. Only for work of 3 or more steps, or several requests in one message. Send the whole list each time, one step in_progress; mark each completed when done. Call it in the same step as your next tool calls, never in a step of its own: each step costs the user seconds. With your last tool calls, mark the work completed and the last step (the answer) in_progress: answering completes it. Every other step ends completed, or cancelled with the reason in its text.

text.description: The step in a few words, in the user's language; for a cancelled step, why

status.description: pending: not started. in_progress: what you are doing now, exactly one at a time. completed: done. cancelled: you will not do it

name: askUserQuestion
description: Ask one question with 2 to 4 answers as buttons; the pick, or the user's own words, comes back as their next message. Use it when the next step depends on a few clear options (a task's setup, which groups or tasks, which match). Open questions (what they offer, a price) stay in your text. It ends your turn, so first write everything the answer has to say (what you found, with links); write the question only here, and call nothing after it.

question.description: The question, in the user's language and voice

options.description: 2 to 4 short answers as the user would say them, the recommended one first
